C1.title: m15's zero-skip gate env var is never registered
C1.resolution: DESKTOP_BUNDLE_GATE added to tests/conftest.py::_DESKTOP_GATE_ENV, arming the zero-skip guard for make desktop-bundle-check. Because this is the THIRD occurrence of one defect (m6 H3 found it unarmed and fixed it; m15 wired the Makefile half and not the conftest half), the fix is guarded rather than just applied: new UNMARKED test_every_desktop_gate_env_var_is_registered_in_conftest DERIVES the DESKTOP_*_GATE set from the Makefile and requires each to appear in the tuple. Verified against its RED state by simulating the pre-fix conftest, where it reports exactly DESKTOP_BUNDLE_GATE missing. The recurrence cause is now stated in the code: the Makefile's -m tautology makes a gate look wired while the skip-to-failure half is absent, and neither file referenced the other

H1.title: AC3's launch claim is unproven at the artifact level
H1.resolution: Roadmap AC3 narrowed to what the gate measures: an assembled, outer-sealed .app whose supervisor resolves its bundled payload, measured against the real artifact. The prior text claimed double-click to a ready server and rendered window, which the --print-child-plan probe does not measure (it resolves and exits without loading models). Disclosing that in an implementation note rather than in the criterion was the same shape as m10's AC1 fixture substitution that m15 was written to retire. What would prove the original claim is recorded, with the reason it is NOT in m15's gate (it would make bundle assembly depend on ~4.6 GB of model weights) and assigned to m11 as a stated obligation

M1.title: the seal's coverage of the payload is claimed but never measured
M1.resolution: New requires_desktop_bundle test measures the seal's COVERAGE instead of asserting it: it copies the bundle, verifies the copy, mutates a byte in the payload executable under Contents/Resources, and requires codesign --verify --strict to change verdict. A seal covering only Contents/MacOS would have passed the previous assertion. Run against a copy so the real artifact is never damaged for later tests in the session

M3.title: one stray cue word disables the notarization-claim scanner
M3.resolution: Notarization scanner tightened three ways: the weak cues (must, may, would, if, open, question) removed so only negations and verbs of forbidding exempt; the cue must now PRECEDE the claim it disclaims, so a trailing cue cannot launder a claim already made; and six phrasings the adversary reached the gate with (will notarize, should/would notarize, notarizable, ready to ship to notary, ready for distribution, satisfies notarization requirements) added to the patterns with eight sentences added to the must-flag corpus. Critique files excluded from the scan set, and only critique files: quoting a forbidden phrase is how a bypass gets reported, and gating that would make the finding unwriteable

M6.title: the quarantine negative has no in-invocation control and its attribution is inferred
M6.resolution: The quarantine negative now runs a SAME-RUN positive control: an unquarantined copy of the same bundle must report through the same open(1) path first, or the test fails naming the harness rather than concluding anything. Without it, no report was indistinguishable from the harness never observing a launch - the permission-denied-as-verified-absence mistake that mis-filed issue #423, which is the same discipline test_supervisor_owns_a_native_window_while_running enforces

M11.title: "raises rather than leaving an unsealed `.app`" is not what the code does
M11.resolution: The unsealed .app is now REMOVED (shutil.rmtree) before the BuildError raises, and the error says so. Three documents claimed assembly raises rather than leaving an unsealed .app; the raise was real, the removal was not, and _app() accepts any directory at that path so the residue was readable as a product. Fixed the behavior rather than weakening the claim, because the claim is the one worth having

M12.title: tauri build inherits an environment that can silently activate Tauri's own signing
M12.resolution: tauri build now runs under _tauri_build_env(), which strips the twelve APPLE_*/TAURI_SIGNING_* variables that make Tauri's bundler sign or notarize on its own. Decision 1 gives signing exclusively to presign_payload + seal_app; an ambient identity would have inserted a second, differently-configured signer between placement and the outer seal while the report still described ours as the only one. Scrubbed rather than asserted absent, so a developer whose shell exports an identity for unrelated work can still build

M13.title: tauri-cli is version-pinned, not hash-pinned, and the difference is unstated
M13.resolution: The version-pin-vs-hash-pin difference is now stated at TAURI_CLI_VERSION: requirements-build.txt provisions PyInstaller under --require-hashes (exact bytes), this is cargo install --locked --version (version plus dependency graph, trusting crates.io immutability). Recorded rather than closed - vendoring the crate or checksumming the built binary is outside m15 - so a reader comparing the two toolchains does not infer parity
